descriptor: An OAuth-style identity and access management system for autonomous AI agents, providing short-lived, narrowly-scoped tokens with human approval and real-time enforcement.

requirements.statement: The system must issue short-lived, narrowly-scoped tokens for AI agents.
The system must allow human approval for every token request via a plain-language consent screen.
The system must enforce that a subagent can only inherit a strict subset of its parent's scope.
The system must validate token scope and revocation status in real-time at the Enforcement Gateway.
The system must log every allowed and blocked action to an immutable audit log.
The system must deny actions when token validity or scope cannot be confirmed.
The system must integrate with mock endpoints for email, code hosting, payment, and CRM systems.
The system must provide a fail-closed circuit-breaker state when the Policy & Token Store is unreachable.
The system must support field-level redaction for customer data access.
The system must provide distinct reason codes for denied actions in the Audit Log.
The system must allow policy definition for token scopes and constraints.
The system must ensure zero instances of a subagent obtaining a scope broader than its parent.
The system must provide a Consent UI for approvers to review and approve token requests.
The system must provide a client SDK for developers to request and present tokens.
The system must ensure that a revoked token's next call fails within the same request cycle.
The system must support anomaly detection for token requests.
The system must provide a mechanism for human policy authorship and approval.
The system must provide error messages for rejected tokens indicating the reason (out of scope, expired, revoked).

stories.title: Issue and enforce a token with audit logging
stories.narrative: As a developer, I want to issue a token and have it enforced, so that I can ensure secure access control for AI agents.
acceptance: Given a token request, when it is approved, then the token is issued and enforced.
Given a revoked token, when it is used, then the action is blocked.
Trust: Every action is logged in the Audit Log.
failure_paths: Token issuance fails due to invalid scope.
Token enforcement fails due to revocation.
Audit log entry fails to record action.
stories.task_guidance: Implement token issuance and enforcement logic. Ensure actions are logged to the Audit Log.

stories.title: Implement real-time revocation handling
stories.narrative: As a security officer, I want revoked tokens to fail immediately, so that unauthorized access is prevented.
acceptance: Given a token, when it is revoked, then its next call fails immediately.
Given a revoked token, when it is used, then the action is blocked.
Trust: Revocation is logged with a reason code.
stories.task_guidance: Ensure the Enforcement Gateway checks revocation status in real-time.

stories.title: Implement Consent UI for token approval
stories.narrative: As an approver, I want to approve token requests via a Consent UI, so that I can control access securely.
acceptance: Given a token request, when it is displayed, then the approver can approve or deny it.
Given a denied request, when it is submitted, then the token is not issued.
Trust: Approval actions are logged.
stories.task_guidance: Develop the Consent UI for token approval and integrate with the token issuance process.

stories.title: Implement delegation narrowing for subagents
stories.narrative: As a security officer, I want subagents to inherit a strict subset of their parent's scope, so that privilege escalation is prevented.
acceptance: Given a subagent request, when it is processed, then it inherits a subset of the parent's scope.
Given a subagent request, when it exceeds the parent's scope, then it is denied.
Trust: Delegation actions are logged.
failure_paths: Subagent inherits full scope instead of subset.
stories.task_guidance: Implement delegation logic to enforce scope narrowing for subagents.

stories.title: Integrate with mock endpoints and deny actions when token validity or scope cannot be confirmed
stories.narrative: As a system administrator, I want the system to deny actions when token validity or scope cannot be confirmed, so that unauthorized actions are prevented.
acceptance: Given a valid token, when the token is used to access a mock endpoint, then the action is allowed.
Given an invalid token, when the token is used to access a mock endpoint, then the action is denied.
Trust: Given any token, when the token is used, then the action and its outcome are logged in the Audit Log.
stories.task_guidance: Ensure integration with mock endpoints includes checks for token validity and scope. Implement logging for all actions and outcomes in the Audit Log.

stories.title: Implement anomaly detection for token requests
stories.narrative: As a security officer, I want to detect anomalies in token requests, so that I can respond to potential security threats.
acceptance: Given a token request, when it is anomalous, then an alert is triggered.
Given a normal request, when it is processed, then no alert is triggered.
Trust: Anomaly detection actions are logged.
failure_paths: Anomaly detection action is not logged.
stories.task_guidance: Develop anomaly detection logic for token requests and integrate with the alerting system.

stories.title: Develop policy management features
stories.narrative: As a policy manager, I want to define token scopes and constraints, so that I can control access policies.
acceptance: Given a policy, when it is created, then it defines token scopes and constraints.
Given a policy, when it is modified, then changes are applied.
Trust: Policy actions are logged.
stories.task_guidance: Implement policy management interface and logic for defining scopes and constraints.

stories.title: Provide a client SDK for token requests
stories.narrative: As a developer, I want a client SDK to request and present tokens, so that I can easily integrate with Ambit.
acceptance: Given a developer, when they use the SDK, then they can request a token.
Given a token request, when it is invalid, then an error is returned.
Trust: SDK usage is logged.
failure_paths: Invalid token request does not return error.
stories.task_guidance: Develop a client SDK for token requests and ensure it handles errors appropriately.

stories.title: Implement fail-closed circuit-breaker for Policy & Token Store
stories.narrative: As a security officer, I want a fail-closed circuit-breaker for the Policy & Token Store, so that I can ensure system security during outages.
acceptance: Given the Policy & Token Store is unreachable, when a request is made, then it is denied.
Given the Store is reachable, when a request is made, then it is processed.
Trust: Circuit-breaker actions are logged.
failure_paths: Request is incorrectly processed during outage.
stories.task_guidance: Implement fail-closed logic for the Policy & Token Store and integrate with the alerting system.

stories.title: Provide detailed error messages for rejected tokens
stories.narrative: As a developer, I want detailed error messages for rejected tokens, so that I can understand why a token was rejected.
acceptance: Given a rejected token, when it is used, then a detailed error message is returned.
Given a valid token, when it is used, then no error message is returned.
Trust: Error message actions are logged.
failure_paths: Error message action is not logged.
stories.task_guidance: Ensure error messages for rejected tokens are detailed and informative.

stories.title: Support field-level redaction for customer data access
stories.narrative: As a data privacy officer, I want field-level redaction for customer data access, so that sensitive information is protected.
acceptance: Given a request for customer data, when the data is accessed, then sensitive fields are redacted.
Given a request for customer data, when the request lacks proper authorization, then access is denied.
Trust: Given any data access, when the data is accessed, then the access and redaction actions are logged in the Audit Log.
stories.task_guidance: Implement field-level redaction in the data access layer. Ensure all access and redaction actions are logged.

stories.title: Provide distinct reason codes for denied actions in the Audit Log
stories.narrative: As a compliance officer, I want distinct reason codes for denied actions in the Audit Log, so that I can understand why actions were denied.
acceptance: Given a denied action, when the action is logged, then a distinct reason code is recorded.
Given a denied action due to token expiration, when the action is logged, then the reason code indicates token expiration.
Trust: Given any denied action, when the action is logged, then the reason code is included in the Audit Log.
stories.task_guidance: Update the Audit Log schema to include reason codes for denied actions. Implement logic to assign reason codes based on denial reasons.
